reading.body:
Ed Pagano is named on 56 AI lobbying filings, and the client list runs from OpenAI and Microsoft to Salesforce, Dropbox, Adobe, Amazon, SAP, and Stack Infrastructure.

The mix is the point. This is not a portfolio of model developers only. It includes application and enterprise software companies, a cloud and infrastructure provider, and a safety policy nonprofit. A single lobbyist carrying filings for both the builders of AI systems and the companies that sell or host them suggests the AI lobbying footprint is consolidating around shared legislative interests rather than splitting along the build-versus-deploy line.

The two bills named, S 3982 and HR 7786, appear only as identifiers with no subject matter attached, so the data cannot say what provisions drew this coalition together. The prior government positions, four Senate and executive branch roles ending between 2004 and 2014, are disclosed because the Lobbying Disclosure Act requires it, and the data draws no connection between those roles and the clients listed.

What this does not cover is timing, spending, or outcome. It counts filings, not dollars, and it says nothing about whether any position advocated was adopted. It also covers one lobbyist, and the summary notes a different lobbyist shares the name, so the 56 filings belong to LDA lobbyist id 71754 alone.

summary: Ed Pagano is named as a lobbyist on 56 Lobbying Disclosure Act filing(s) about AI held by this site. The firms, clients and AI bills on those filings are below. LDA lobbyist id 71754. A different lobbyist with the same name has a separate page.
